articles.title: Reality check after Commonwealth Games 2026: Indiaâs boxing renaissance to face ultimate Asian exam
articles.summary: Commonwealth Games News: NEW DELHI: Indiaâs record-breaking boxing campaign at the Commonwealth Games has generated plenty of optimism, but the celebrations will quickly give .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Indiaâs record-breaking boxing campaign at the Commonwealth Games has generated plenty of optimism, but the celebrations will quickly give way to a far sterner test when attention shifts to the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, from Sept 19 to Oct 4. After returning from Glasgow with a historic haul of seven gold and three silver medals, Indiaâs boxers now head into what many within the sport regard as the closest thing to the Olympics.The CWG triumph underlined the countryâs growing depth, particularly in womenâs boxing. Sakshi Chaudhary (51kg), Preeti Pawar (54kg), Jaismine Lamboria (57kg), Priya Ghanghas (60kg) and Arundhati Choudhary (70kg) struck gold, while Sachin Siwach (60kg) and Ankush Panghal (80kg) topped the podium in the menâs competition. Olympic medallist Lovlina Borgohain, Jadumani Singh and Narender Berwal added silver medals.The challenge in Aichi-Nagoya, however, will be on an entirely different scale. Unlike the Commonwealth Games, the Asian Games will feature continental powerhouses such as Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, China, Chinese Taipei, Japan and North Korea â nations that have consistently dominated the World Championships and the Olympics. Uzbek stars Mirazizbek Mirzakhalilov and Bobo-Usmon Baturov, along with Kazakhstanâs Kairat Yeraliyev and Ablaikhan Zhussupov, are expected to headline a field packed with world-class talent.India will also be without two of its Commonwealth champions. Jaismine (57kg) and Arundhati (70kg) will miss out because their weight categories do not feature in the Asian Games programme, depriving the country of two genuine medal prospects.âThe Asian Games for us is like the Olympics,â Boxing Federation of India president Ajay Singh said. âThe best teams in the world today are Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and India, and all three are in Asia. Add a strong Chinese contingent and you understand why it is much tougher. You canât replicate this (CWG) performance at the Asian Games. But if you win a sizeable number of medals at the Asian Games, you can be hopeful of winning medals at the Olympics too.âWomenâs head coach Santiago Nieva shared a similar assessment while insisting the team remains on the right path.âWe canât guarantee that we will win gold all the time, but we are on the right track. We know how strong the field will be at the Asian Games. The boxers are aware that they canât sit on their success,â he said.India had returned with one silver and three bronze medals from the 2022 Asian Games in Hangzhou. The Glasgow CWG showcased the strides the boxing contingent has made. But itâll be Aichi-Nagoya that is going to reveal whether the progress is enough to challenge Asiaâs finest and signal genuine medal potential for the 2028 Olympics.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: Neeraj Chopra has opened up about the emotional journey behind his silver medal at the Commonwealth Games 2026, saying the achievement means much more than the distance he threw. The Olympic champion, who returned after battling multiple injuries, shared a heartfelt message on Instagram along with pictures and videos from Glasgow.The Indian javelin star said the last 10 months were extremely difficult and thanked everyone who helped him during his recovery.Chopra secured the silver medal with a best throw of 85.83m, while debutant Yashvir Singh won bronze as India celebrated two medals in the event.Chopra's final attempt ended in a foul, but his earlier effort was enough to seal second place in his second Commonwealth Games appearance."There are throws that travel far, and then there are moments that carry the weight of an entire journey. This one means so much more than the distance," Chopra said.ID@undefined Caption not available.ID@undefined Caption not available.ID@undefined Caption not available."The past 10 months has tested me in ways I never expected. articles.title: Glasgow to Ahmedabad: Gujarat receives Commonwealth Games flag as 2030 countdown begins
articles.summary: Commonwealth Games News: The Commonwealth Games flag was formally presented to Gujarat chief minister Bhupendra Patel on Wednesday, marking the beginning of preparations for t.
articles.body: The Commonwealth Games flag was formally presented to Gujarat chief minister Bhupendra Patel on Wednesday, marking the beginning of preparations for the 2030 Commonwealth Games in Ahmedabad.After returning from Glasgow, deputy chief minister Harsh Sanghavi handed over the flag to Patel during the state cabinet meeting in Gandhinagar.Sanghavi had attended the closing ceremony of the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow on Sunday along with Olympic champion Neeraj Chopra and Indian Olympic Association (IOA) president PT Usha. During the ceremony, the Commonwealth Games flag was officially handed over to India as Ahmedabad prepares to host the next edition in 2030.According to an official release, "deputy chief minister Harsh Sanghavi formally presented the Commonwealth Games Flag, with full honour and dignity, to chief minister Bhupendra Patel during the state cabinet meeting in Gandhinagar."Para-athletes Rakesh Bhatt and Rohit Majgul, who represented Gujarat at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games, were present during the ceremony. Para table tennis player Sonal Patel also attended.The release added, "The Commonwealth Games Flag will now remain in Gujarat until the 2030 Commonwealth Games. Along with advancing Prime Minister Narendra Modi's 'Fit India' vision, it will serve as an inspiration for athletes and symbolise the commencement of preparations for the upcoming event."Speaking to reporters after arriving at Ahmedabad Airport earlier in the day, Sanghavi said the city aims to set a new standard for hosting the Commonwealth Games."These Games will be organised with grandeur and with the best possible arrangements for the athletes. They will be conducted in such a way that every athlete can deliver his best performance," the deputy CM said.Sanghavi, who also holds the sports portfolio, said the Gujarat government remains committed to taking forward Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Fit India movement and anti-drug campaign."We will advance the anti-drug campaign and the Fit India Movement so that the youth of the country receive maximum opportunities in the sports sector. The Gujarat Government is working towards this goal. Under the guidance of the Government of India, we will continue to move this work forward," he said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Commonwealth Games News: Pakistanâs Olympic javelin champion Arshad Nadeem has blamed the cold Glasgow weather for his disappointing performance at the Commonwealth Games. The.
articles.body: Pakistanâs Olympic javelin champion Arshad Nadeem has blamed the cold Glasgow weather for his disappointing performance at the Commonwealth Games. The defending champion finished ninth after failing to make the final three rounds, saying the low temperature made his body stiff and affected his usually smooth run-up.Nadeem managed 77.41 metres with his second throw after opening with a foul. His third attempt was 75.39m, leaving him outside the top eight.âThe weather was extremely cold and I personally felt that it affected my body. As you have seen in many of my previous competitions, my run-up is usually very smooth, but this time it wasnâtâ¦ because my body had become stiff due to the cold conditions. My fitness was good and my health was fine, but ultimately whatever Allah wills is what happens,â he told reporters on Wednesday.Despite the result, Nadeem said he remains determined to make a strong comeback and urged fans to continue supporting him.âPlease donât lose heart and donât stop supporting me either. Whatever I have achieved has only been possible because Allah blessed me with the opportunity to do it. The respect and recognition Pakistan has received around the world have come through years of hard work. I worked tirelessly while staying in Pakistan,â he added.âGod willing, I will prepare with full dedication for the upcoming competitions and once again raise Pakistanâs flag on the international stage.âNadeem also responded to criticism on social media, saying he understood the disappointment among Pakistani fans.âI have heard many things on social media, but I want everyone to remember that I am Pakistanâs son, and I always will be,â he maintained.Lausanne Diamond League nextNadeemâs next challenge will be the Lausanne Diamond League in Switzerland on August 21. He will face a strong field that includes Indiaâs Neeraj Chopra, Commonwealth champion Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage, Keshorn Walcott, Anderson Peters and Thomas Rohler.Nadeem will hope to regain his form before the Asian Games later this year.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Parker’s positive cocaine test caused by nutritionist, doping body says
articles.summary: The 34-year-old boxer tested positive for cocaine on day of shock loss to Fabio Wardley in London in October.
articles.body:
Former world heavyweight boxing champion Joseph Parker has been cleared to return to the ring after serving a three-month drugs ban that authorities said was due to his nutritionist.

The 34-year-old New Zealander tested positive for cocaine on the day of his shock loss to Fabio Wardley in London in October.

Parker has always denied knowingly taking any banned substances and United Kingdom Anti-Doping (UKAD) said the nutritionist he employed ahead of his fight with Wardley was a “regular user of cocaine”.

“New Zealand professional boxer Joseph Parker has served a three-month ban from all World Anti-Doping Code-compliant sport following an anti-doping rule violation (ADRV) for the presence of a prohibited substance,” a UKAD statement said on Thursday.

“At the time of this announcement, Mr Parker is free to participate in sport.”

“On 6 March 2026, Mr Parker provided UKAD with evidence claiming that the adverse analytical finding was the result of his exposure to cocaine used by the nutritionist he had employed in preparation for the bout on 25 October 2025.

“The nutritionist stated that he was a regular user of cocaine and had used cocaine daily in the week leading up to the bout,” the statement added.

Parker was tested by the Voluntary Anti-Doping Association (VADA) on October 25.

On the same day, he was beaten by Briton Wardley at London’s O2 Arena.

Parker failed a UKAD test in the early hours of October 26 .

UKAD added it had found in June that Parker’s cocaine ingestion had occurred out of competition and therefore was “in a context unrelated to sport performance”, thereby lifting his previous suspension.

Parker’s professional record stands at 36 wins and four defeats.

He was WBO heavyweight champion from 2016 to 2018 before losing the title to Britain’s Anthony Joshua in Cardiff.

UKAD’s statement came the day after Parker himself announced his ban had been lifted.

“I’m pleased to confirm my provisional suspension is lifted and I’ll be back in the ring soon,” he said.

Parker suffered an 11th-round stoppage defeat by Wardley and lost his status as WBO mandatory challenger to then undisputed heavyweight champion Oleksandr Usyk.

articles.title: How Harsh fought through pain to script CWG history, now targets Asiad medal
articles.summary: Commonwealth Games News: NEW DELHI: Harsh Singh's right knee still swells. It still hurts. Every time the Indian judoka steps onto the mat, he is reminded of the ACL and menis.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Harsh Singh's right knee still swells. It still hurts. Every time the Indian judoka steps onto the mat, he is reminded of the ACL and meniscus tear that nearly derailed his career. But at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, pain took a back seat as the 23-year-old scripted history by becoming India's first-ever men's judo gold medallist."The pain never really goes away," Singh told TOI in an interview on Thursday. "Sometimes my knee still swells up and feels tight. During the CWG, I felt the pain and the knee occasionally got swollen. After surgery, the joint never became exactly the way it was before. There's always a little discomfort during fights. You have to ignore it and continue. The medal kept me going."The historic triumph came less than a year after Singh tore his ACL and meniscus while training at the Inspire Institute of Sport (IIS) in Aug 2025. Surgery followed in Oct last in Bengaluru before a year-long rehabilitation helped him return to competition."I was in rehabilitation for almost a year. The entire coaching team at the IIS, recovery specialists and Spencer sir (Mackay, S&C expert) helped me throughout. They rebuilt my strength step by step. Because of the IIS and their entire team, I was able to come back on the mat, qualify for the CWG and represent India," he said.The comeback demanded another battle off the mat. Months away from competition saw his weight rise to nearly 72kg, forcing him to shed more than 12kg to return to his 60kg category. Gold at a ranking tournament and bronze at the senior National championships sealed his place in India's CWG squad.Despite lingering discomfort, Singh dominated in Glasgow, with only a hard-fought semifinal stretching him before he clinched the historic title."The semifinal (against the Australian Pedro Carlos) was the toughest. In the 60kg category, even a small point can decide the match. We didn't want to concede anything and stayed aggressive," he recalled.With CWG gold secured, Singh has already shifted his attention to next year's Asian Games. Training stints in Japan and South Korea are part of his preparations as he looks to bridge the gap with Asia's best."I want to improve my speed, grip and strength. Japanese and Korean players are very fast, so training there will help," he said.Born into a modest family, with his father working as a daily-wage labourer, Singh once trained without owning a judo uniform. Support from the govt's schemes and a privately funded athletes' training centre changed the course of his career."My life has changed because of this medal. More people have started noticing judo," he said. "But the best compliment came from my family. They told me, 'You have made the entire family proud.' That meant more than anything else."Having conquered injury to create CWG history, Singh's next aim is clear â turning a gritty comeback into an Asian Games podium finish.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Days after historic CWG gold, Dilip Gavit leaves without meeting Raj Thackeray after two-hour wait
articles.summary: Commonwealth Games News: Just days after scripting history for Indian para athletics at the Commonwealth Games, gold medallist Dilip Gavit found himself making headlines for a.
articles.body: Just days after scripting history for Indian para athletics at the Commonwealth Games, gold medallist Dilip Gavit found himself making headlines for a very different reason. The 23-year-old sprinter, who became India's first-ever Commonwealth Games gold medallist in the men's 100m T47 event, waited for nearly two hours to meet Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) chief Raj Thackeray in Nashik on Thursday before leaving without the meeting taking place.Invited, but left waitingAccording to Gavit's coach quoted by PTI, Vaijanath Kale, the para-athlete had been invited to meet Thackeray during the MNS chief's visit to Nashik. However, despite arriving at the scheduled venue, Gavit and his coach were made to wait for nearly two hours. A video from the venue showed MNS workers requesting the duo to wait longer while trying to explain that Thackeray was occupied."We were waiting for quite some time... Sir is busy. We will meet him later," Kale is heard saying in the video before they eventually left.A champion who made history in GlasgowThe incident came just days after Gavit delivered one of India's biggest moments at the Commonwealth Games. Clocking a Games-record 10.71 seconds, the Nashik sprinter won the men's 100m T47 gold medal, leading a historic Indian one-two finish alongside Mohammed Basil Morssinganakath, who claimed silver. The victory marked India's first-ever Commonwealth Games gold medal in para athletics 100m T47.A journey built on resilienceGavit's success carries a deeper significance given his remarkable journey. Born into an economically disadvantaged tribal family in Maharashtra, he lost his right arm in a childhood accident. His life changed when coach Vaijanath Kale took him under his wing at the age of 12, supporting his education and athletic development. After winning gold in Glasgow, Gavit emotionally dedicated the medal to Kale, crediting his coach for transforming his life.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Raymond van Barneveld fined and suspended over inappropriate behaviour and offensive language in latest Darts Regulation Authority case list
articles.summary: Dutch darts legend Raymond van Barneveld, Cameron Menzies and Dom Taylor are among the high-profile players named in the latest Darts Regulation Authority (DRA) case list, published for the first time since 2022
articles.body:
The DRA, which is the independent body responsible for regulating the sport, particularly in events run under the umbrella of the PDC, WDF, Modus and ADC, has published an updated case list for the first time since 2022, listing all backdated hearings from January 2023 to June 2026, relating to various incidents that had occurred in both televised and non-televised competition.

Former world champions Rob Cross, Gary Anderson, Luke Humphries and Van Barneveld all feature in the case list, along with Cameron Menzies and Dom Taylor.

Van Barneveld, widely regarded as one of the sport's greatest-ever players, features in two separate incidents.

The first involves 'Inappropriate behaviour and using offensive language' at Players Championship 2 event in Wigan last year, resulting in a three-month suspension [suspended for 12 months] and £3,000 fine.

The second relates to 'failing to report damage caused to hotel room' following a Players Championship event in Germany, which resulted in a formal warning.

'Barney' is a five-time world champion having won the BDO tournament at Lakeside in 1998, 1999, 2003 and 2005 before making the move to the PDC the following year.

The doyen of Dutch darts made his mark by winning the 2007 PDC World Championship with a legendary final against Phil 'The Power' Taylor.

Sky Sports have contacted the DRA regarding Van Barneveld's fines.

Menzies' sanction for his outburst at the World Championship in December has been revealed , with the Scot handed a four-month suspension, which ended last month, and receiving a £2,500 fine after he repeatedly punched the underside of the drinks' table on stage in frustration following his defeat to Charlie Manby.

The incident drew blood on his knuckles, which he then wiped on his face before walking off the stage.

Shortly after the incident, Menzies issued a statement apologising for his actions.

"First of all, I would like to apologise for what happened," said Menzies. "I am sorry that I reacted in the manner that I did.

"It's not an excuse, but I have had a lot of things on my mind recently and I suppose it all just became too much at the end.

"It has not been an easy time for me with my uncle Gary passing away recently. I saw him four days before he died and he gave a look which told he much he thought of me. He treated me like a son.

"Had I won the game against Charlie, my second match would have been on the day of Gary's funeral and that has not been lost on me in recent days.

"Let me say again, that's no excuse for what I did on the stage. It was the wrong thing to do and I don't want it to take anything away from Charlie. He played well and deserved his win.

"This is not how I would like people to view me. Yes I can get emotional at times, but not like that and that wasn't right."

Taylor's failed drugs test at the World Championship resulted in a six-month suspension until June 18 , as well as a £1,275 fine in costs and the forfeiture of his £25,000 in prize money.

Taylor tested positive for cocaine and cannabis with the offence being his second which incurred a mandatory six-month ban under DRA rules.

"Accordingly, and taking into account all of the available evidence, the committee were satisfied that Mr Taylor's ingestion of both cocaine and cannabis occurred out of competition and was not following the commencement of the World Championship on 11th December 2025," the DRA statement read.

"Following on from this finding, the committee has determined that as this is Mr Taylor's second offence, then under these rules, he must serve a six month ban in line with 10.9 (a) and 10.9 (b) of UKAD Anti-Doping Rules 2021".

Taylor also lost his Tour Card as a result of the offence.

He had previously served a one-month ban in 2025 after failing a drugs test at the Players Championship Finals in November 2024. The ban was reduced from an initial two years after he agreed to undergo a UKAD-approved three-month substance abuse treatment programme.

Prakash Jiwa and Andy Jenkins both received hefty bans and were each made to pay costs of over £17,000 after being found guilty of match-fixing in the Modus Super Series from 2022-2023.

articles.title: How Jadumani Singh's risky weight change nearly derailed his CWG dream before winning Glasgow silver
articles.summary: Commonwealth Games News: NEW DELHI: When Indian pugilist Jadumani Singh Mandengbam stepped onto the podium to receive the men's 55kg silver medal at the 2026 Commonwealth Game.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: When Indian pugilist Jadumani Singh Mandengbam stepped onto the podium to receive the men's 55kg silver medal at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, it marked the culmination of a journey that had almost ended before it had even begun.The 22-year-old Manipuri boxer was one of India's standout performers, winning four consecutive unanimous 5-0 verdicts to storm into the bantamweight final before settling for silver against Australia's Jye Dixon. His medal also formed part of India's historic boxing campaign, which yielded seven golds and three silvers, making the country the No. 1 boxing nation at the Games for the first time.Yet, behind that success lay months of uncertainty, selection hurdles and a weight-category gamble that nearly cost him a place on the flight to Scotland.Speaking exclusively to TimesofIndia.com, former world champion and Jadumani's mentor, Laishram Sarita Devi, recounted how the young boxer refused to abandon his Olympic dream even when every obstacle seemed stacked against him.A bold gamble after the 50kg category disappearedJadumani had built his reputation in the 50kg category, winning medals at World Boxing Cups before learning that the division would no longer feature in the Commonwealth Games, Asian Games or Olympic programme.Rather than remain in a non-Olympic category, he decided to move up to 55kg â a division already occupied by some of India's biggest names."He continued to consult with me. Whenever he had to make a big decision, he called up and consulted with me â like increasing his weight category," Sarita told TimesofIndia.com."After he won a World Cup medal in 50kg, he got to know that the weight category is no longer in the CWG, Asian Games and Olympics. He wanted to move to 55kg."The decision immediately brought fresh challenges."Army had their No. 1 boxer in the 55kg category in Pune, who is Services' No. 1 boxer. And the weight category also has Amit Panghal â Olympian and Asian champion. He said he wanted to move up the weight to compete at CWG, Asian Games etc, but was discouraged by hearing questions like whether he would be able to compete at that level, which created a doubt in him," she said.Sarita, however, wanted only one answer: "We sat down and I asked him, 'Are you confident about the decision?' He said he was, so I told him to move up the category."The selection maze before GlasgowThe decision created another problem.Without competing in the National Championships, Jadumani could not enter the national coaching camp. But because he belonged to the Army Sports Institute, Services already had its designated 55kg representative. Attempts to let him represent Manipur also failed."We tried to make him compete for the state of Manipur, but we didn't get an NOC because he is with the Army," Sarita said.Relief finally arrived through a Boxing Federation of India (BFI) policy that granted direct entries to the National Championships for World Boxing Cup medallists. The move was aimed at rewarding elite international performers and ensuring they were not blocked by the usual domestic qualification pathways.The decision allowed Jadumani to compete directly in the 55kg draw despite the institutional overlap, resulting in multiple squad members â Pawan Bartwal, Jadumani Singh and Amit Panghal â finding themselves in the same weight-category draw.Sarita said her ward grabbed the opportunity with both hands."He then got a chance to compete in 55kg in the Nationals. Due to his effort, he won against the Services No.1, Olympians etc to be named Best Boxer in the Nationals. After that he got the chance to be part of the India camp," she said.He then cleared the final selection trials, which included physical assessments alongside ring performances."He participated in the final trial for the CWG and Asian Games â which had many aspects like strength and endurance tests before fighting in the ring. He won all of it to get selected for the CWG and was really happy and started training hard," she added.The Sports Ministry hurdleJust when Glasgow appeared certain, another setback emerged.Because Jadumani had only recently moved into 55kg, he did not possess the Asian ranking required under the Sports Ministry's eligibility criteria for Commonwealth Games selection."He got an explanation mail from the Sports Ministry, which put him in immense tension ahead of the Games," Sarita recalled.Under the ministry's guidelines, boxers were expected to be ranked among Asia's top eight in their respective categories."He was ranked No. 2 in 50kg, but he lacked a ranking in the new 55kg category. He had only competed in one Asian Championship in the new weight category before the trials for CWG and, being new to the category, lost in the quarterfinals," she said.That led to fresh doubts over his selection."He was disheartened when questions were raised whether he was a medal prospect because he was not in the rankings prescribed by the ministry. He called me and said the coaches were saying he may or may not be on the flight to the CWG because of this letter from the ministry," she recalled.The uncertainty only ended after BFI submitted a detailed explanation to the ministry, outlining Jadumani's circumstances following his weight-category switch."BFI replied to the ministry properly, explaining everything and after a lot of effort his ticket to Glasgow was approved. What I like about him is that he is the kind of person who doesn't give up and has a very strong will power," she said.Why the gold slipped awayJadumani eventually reached the final after four demanding contests, each won by an identical 5-0 margin. But Sarita believes the scheduling ultimately worked against him."Jadumani's four bouts were very tough. He played all out in all the bouts till the semifinals as he got proper rest and recovery time. Since the gold medal opponent got a bye earlier, he had fewer bouts than Jadumani," she explained.The semifinal-final turnaround, she felt, proved decisive. There was a one-day gap after every bout until the semifinals, but there was no gap between the semifinal and final in Glasgow."Jadumani fought his semifinal in the evening and got the final bout the next morning only, so he did not get much time for recovery. If it was in the evening, he could have fought better. When he entered the ring for the final, I saw his face and body language sitting here and realised he had not had enough recovery," she said.The experience, she believes, underlines the growing importance of sports science."In such situations, we should look for how we can enhance or speed up the recovery process through sports science. We should discuss it to make sure our boxers can give 100 per cent every time they enter the ring," she added.Olympic gold remains the ultimate dreamSarita first noticed Jadumani as a youngster competing in a local tournament."When I saw Jadumani for the first time, it was a tournament for young boys. His movement was really pleasing and I thought he could become a good boxer in the future. I identified him at that time only and gave him Rs 500 because I was very pleased with his performance," she recalled."Jadumani did not start with me from the grassroots. He learnt his basics from another academy. He came to my academy when he was preparing to enrol in the Army Sports Institute in Pune. At that time, I did not have any infrastructure and was coaching from a makeshift setup. And then Covid happened, we had to train in a very isolated small makeshift place,â she added.Years later, after training together through difficult Covid-19 conditions and watching him overcome one hurdle after another, Sarita believes Glasgow is only the beginning."We missed gold at the CWG, but we will work hard to get gold at the Asian Games for sure," she said.The bigger ambition, however, stretches far beyond continental success."His first and primary target remains Olympic gold. Commonwealth Games and Asian Games are the stepping stones in that journey. He will try to win India's first Olympic gold medal in boxing," Sarita concluded.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: From hospital bed to CWG gold: How Jaismine Lamboria fought the odds in Glasgow
articles.summary: Commonwealth Games News: NEW DELHI: Just weeks before stepping into the ring at the Commonwealth Games, Jaismine Lamboria wasnât thinking about medals. She was searching for a.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Just weeks before stepping into the ring at the Commonwealth Games, Jaismine Lamboria wasnât thinking about medals. She was searching for answers. The recurring fever had refused to go away.Multiple medical tests showed nothing unusual and the Indian boxer tried to push through, managing the symptoms with paracetamol. When the illness persisted, she was admitted to a hospital in Mohali. Doctors finally diagnosed a bacterial infection, putting her on an intensive 14-day course of medication. For an athlete preparing for one of the biggest competitions of the year, it could easily have been the end of the campaign.Instead, it became the beginning of one of the most remarkable comebacks of her career. âI was avoiding further medical tests because the initial reports were coming back normal. We didnât know what exactly had to be treated. Finally, after I was admitted, they detected a bacterial infection and I was on medication for 14 days,â the 57kg boxer said.When she was discharged, the clock was already ticking. Barely three weeks remained before the Games. âI started training only on July 1. Initially it was just warm-up, walking and stretching. I had very little time, so we had to be patient.âThe physical recovery was only one part of the challenge. During those uncertain weeks, sports psychologist Priya Vrinda became a constant source of support, ensuring the illness didnât break her confidence.âWhen I was sick, I was already connected with Priya Vrinda maâam. She kept me mentally strong and never allowed me to go down,â Jaismine said. That resilience was evident when she returned to competition. Jaismine boxed with maturity, tactical discipline and composure to upgrade the Commonwealth bronze she had won four years ago into gold in the 57kg.One of Jaismineâs biggest assets inside the ring has been her reach in her category. While every opponent may not be shorter â Jaismine stands five feet seven inches in her socks â she believes her physical advantage has become an important weapon thanks to careful coaching. âMy coaches taught me how to use my reach properly. articles.body: NEW DELHI: âFrom every drop of tears, gold medals are dripping.âPrime Minister Narendra Modi had an emotional message for Mirabai Chanu as he interacted with India's Commonwealth Games 2026 medal winners at his residence on Sunday, reflecting on the sacrifices behind the country's successful campaign in Glasgow.Modi hosted the medal-winning contingent at 7, Lok Kalyan Marg and heard athletes recount some of the moments that defined their journeys at the Games. India returned from Glasgow with 39 medals, including 13 gold, 17 silver and nine bronze, finishing fourth in the overall standings.During one of the conversations, Modi recalled the emotional scenes surrounding Mirabai's gold-medal triumph.âTears were falling from you. I feel as if from every drop of tears, gold medals are dripping,â Modi told the Olympic silver medallist.Mirabai recalls four years of struggleMirabai, who won gold in Glasgow, opened up about the difficult journey that preceded her Commonwealth Games triumph, including the disappointment of the Paris Olympics.âI was very happy, and emotional too. That day the happiness was greater and I cried because at the Paris Olympics, I lost a medal by 1 kg. In a playerâs life what all we have to face. So within these 4 years, how much and what all I had faced, every time injuries were going on and all that was happening. So with great difficulty I had faced these 4 years. So when all that happened, on the podium when I stood, sir, and when our flag goes up and our national anthem plays, sir, we cannot stop, sir, tears come out on their own,â she said.Modi responded by highlighting the wider impact of the athletes' achievements.âThis is very good. It is not as if this achievement of yours is considered only your achievement; your victory becomes a very big inspiration for the coming generations.ââOne family will bring three medalsâThe informal interaction also saw athletes share lighter and deeply personal moments from their Glasgow campaigns.Modi reminded para shot put gold medallist Sharmila Dhankar of a promise she had made earlier.âYou made a promise. Last time, yours, both daughters will become players,â Modi said with a smile.Dhankar replied: âHaanji, right now they are young in age. In the next Commonwealth, one family will bring 3 medals.âMen's 100m T47 gold medallist Dilip Gavit, meanwhile, spoke about dedicating his performance to his guru.âWhen I was running, when my event was on 29th (July), that day was Guru Purnima, so that day I gave a gift to my guru,â he was heard saying in the video.In another video posted by Modi, gold medallist boxer Sakshi Chaudhary introduced herself and the contingent.âHello friends! This is Sakshi Chaudhary. Today, our honourable Prime Minister has invited us, the Commonwealth Games medalists, and we feel very proud. We are extremely happy to have met him; he is very humble. Sir, would you like to say something?â she said.Modi replied with a message that summed up his interaction with the athletes: âJo khelega, woh khilegaâ (The one who plays, will blossom). âAlways cheer for Bharat.âIndiaâs Glasgow successIndia's fourth-place finish came despite a significantly smaller contingent and a reduced sporting programme compared to Birmingham 2022. India sent 122 athletes to Glasgow, compared to 210 in Birmingham, while 30 of its 61 medals in 2022 came in sports that were not part of the Glasgow programme.Despite those limitations, India retained its fourth-place position and improved its medal conversion rate, with 38 athletes returning home with medals. articles.title: âThat video was not ordinaryâ: PM Modi praises Lovlina for objecting to distorted India map - Watch
articles.summary: Commonwealth Games News: NEW DELHI: Boxer Lovlina Borgohain's decision to object to a distorted Indian map during the Commonwealth Games earned special appreciation from Prime.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Boxer Lovlina Borgohain's decision to object to a distorted Indian map during the Commonwealth Games earned special appreciation from Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who described the moment as one that would be remembered for a long time.Lovlina, who won silver in the women's 75kg category in Glasgow, was among India's medal winners who interacted with Modi at his residence on Sunday. The meeting, attended by Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya, Minister of State for Sports Raksha Khadse and Indian Olympic Association president PT Usha, saw athletes recount their experiences from the Games in an informal and emotional setting.In a little over 10-minute video of the interaction shared by the Prime Minister's Office on Monday, Modi brought up Lovlina's confrontation with a restaurant in Glasgow after she noticed a distorted Indian map.âKya hua wo restaurant waale se jhagda kar rahi thi? (What happened, you were fighting with that restaurant guy?)â Modi asked.Lovlina laughed before explaining why she intervened.âWe had such a good performance and it was the last day of the Games. It was a happy occasion sir, we were celebrating and I didn't like it when I saw the distorted map. I politely told them and they have made the changes also,â she explained.âThat video was not ordinaryâModi applauded the boxer for noticing the issue despite being in the middle of celebrations after her medal-winning campaign.âTo be able to recognise the significance of that map at a time when you were celebrating and the Games were over, I can tell you truthfully, that video was not ordinary. It will be remembered by people for a very long time,â he told the Tokyo Olympics bronze medallist.India finished fourth in Glasgow with 39 medals, including 13 golds, with boxing contributing seven gold medals.The interaction also provided an emotional window into Mirabai Chanu's journey to her gold medal in the women's 48kg category. The weightlifter produced a Games-record lift of 190kg, but her triumph came after four difficult years following her one-kilogram miss at the Paris Olympics.Mirabai opens up about four difficult yearsModi asked Mirabai about the tears she shed on the podium and even fed her a laddu during their interaction.âItne aansu tapak rahe the (So many tears were rolling down),â Modi remarked.Mirabai explained that the tears represented years of accumulated emotions.âI was very happy and emotional at that moment. I was crying because I missed a medal in the Paris Olympics by one kilogram. I have faced a lot in these last four years. I was battling injuries and some family problems too.âThere were a lot of things. So, these four years were very tough for me. And when I stood on the podium, our flag went up and the anthem played, it was hard to stop myself,â she said.Narender's joke leaves Modi laughingThe meeting also had its lighter moments. Boxer Narender Berwal, who won silver in the +90kg category, recalled a funny exchange with a Pakistani boxer after beating him at the 2015 World Military Games.âDuring the 2015 World Military Games, I had a bout with a Pakistani boxer. I won it but when we were together in the medical room for treatment to our niggles, he said to me 'Bhaijan aapka naam Narender hai, aapke coach ka naam Narender hai, aapke Pradhan Mantri ka naam Narender hai, mujhe Narender naam se nafrat ho gayi hai.' (Brother, you, your coach and your PM are all named Narender. I hate this name now),â he recalled, drawing laughter from Modi.The Prime Minister also underlined the broader significance of the athletes' achievements, saying their medals were helping inspire a new generation.âI have been in this house for 12-13 years now and if there is one group that I have met regularly here, it is the athletes because of your efforts to win medals for India and your tradition of scaling new heights.âFar more than our push to promote sports in schools, it is your medals that inspire people,â Modi said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Super League's Final Charge: Leeds Rhinos, Wakefield Trinity, Wigan Warriors, Warrington Wolves, Hull KR, Leigh Leopards and St Helens in contention
articles.summary: A look at the 'Final Charge' and how the last three rounds of the Super League season are shaping up; round 25 of Super League commences from Thursday August 27, live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
In Super League, the two teams who finish first and second are guaranteed a home semi-final across Friday September 25 and Saturday September 26.

In the week prior to that, the Play-Off Eliminators occur in which the third-place team takes on the team in sixth and fourth plays fifth for the chance to make it into the semis.

Then the winners of the semi-finals head to the Grand Final at Old Trafford on Saturday October 3.

Let's take a look at what each team has remaining and what is on the line for them...

Leeds Rhinos have been at the summit of Super League for a while now and they will want to hold onto that for their three remaining fixtures.

However, they are now level on points with Wigan, who briefly leapfrogged them with Friday's win over Wakefield, but they have a vastly-superior points difference after Sunday's rout of York.

They last won the League Leaders' Shield way back in 2015 and last won a trophy in 2020 when they took Challenge Cup glory, so finishing top would see a welcome return of some silverware for the Rhinos.

In their last three matches, they face St Helens (A), Wigan Warriors (A) and Hull FC (H).

After the tricky trip to face Saints, they crucially host the Warriors on September 5 so their run-in is far from an easy on, but if they can now remain unbeaten, League Leaders' Shield glory will be theirs and they will be one match from walking out at the 'Theatre of Dreams' once again.

The team who have been there, done that, and got the T-shirt. Matt Peet, head coach of Wigan, has made no secret of how hard he has been pushing for a top-two finish because he knows how crucial that home semi-final is.

Now, if his team continue on, they could usurp Leeds if they keep the pressure on with their play-off spot confirmed.

Not only that, the Warriors will be hungry to avenge their Grand Final defeat to Hull KR in 2025.

They have the Challenge Cup in their trophy cabinet and will have all eyes on adding a second piece of silverware.

Ahead of the play-offs, they still have to play Hull KR (H), Leeds Rhinos (A) and Catalans Dragons (H).

Warrington Wolves made it three wins in a jam-packed 10 days by beating Huddersfield Giants to move on to 36 points.

Their 34-24 triumph against Huddersfield on Sunday was a fifth consecutive win, putting them in the right form at the right time for the play-off charge with just three rounds to go, and they could yet even snatch top spot.

In their remaining fixtures, they face Hull FC (A), Wakefield Trinity (A) and Toulouse Olympique (H).

All of those teams are below them in the table - a luxury not afforded to many other teams in the play-off picture.

The game against Wakefield will be the toughest test, with Trinity just four points below them.

What a season it has been for Wakefield Trinity.

They are on the hunt for their highest Super League finish, but will now want to bounce back following their heart-breaking two-point defeat to top-of-the-table Leeds and then subsequent defeats to St Helens and Wigan Warriors.

In honesty, with two top teams remaining in their run-in, those results should worry Daryl Powell's side.

They have games against York Knights (H), Warrington Wolves (H) and Leigh Leopards (A) left.

Those are against two teams out of the seven still in the fight.

The team that has become renowned for coming good when they need to, Leigh Leopards want to shore up their spot in the play-offs once again.

After a disastrous start to the season, Adrian Lam's side have found their groove, made waves and look in real good nick at present.

Indeed, their win over Leeds set down a marker.

However, they have a tough end to the season in which they will know every win will matter.

The Leopards face Huddersfield Giants (A), St Helens (H) and Wakefield Trinity (H).

If Leigh want to make it to the Grand Final for the first time, they need to continue to show their steel now.

Hull KR are right in the mix and will want it to stay that way but after their loss to Warrington, they are two points off fourth spot with three games left.

The Robins were the team who did it all in 2025, ending the wait for a new team to win the competition, and now they will want to send coach Willie Peters out on a high by going back to back.

Their shock loss to Toulouse did not help their cause, though.

Their remaining matches are against Wigan Warriors (A), Huddersfield Giants (H) and St Helens (A).

St Helens have three matches to try and ensure they do not make some unwanted history.

Saints have never missed out on the play-offs. Most recently they lost 20-12 to Hull KR in the semi-finals in 2025 as the Robins went on to complete the treble.

After their loss to Hull FC, St Helens looked down and out. With triumphant wins over Wakefield and Castleford, the never-say-die attitude has been reinstated once again.

They will now refocus and aim for three wins out of three to be in with a shout. If they win all three they move to 34 points.

Not only that, they face other teams in the play-off hunt and will take on Leeds Rhinos (H), Leigh Leopards (A) and Hull KR (H).

All three their three remaining matches are against teams in the top six - talk about having to take your moment.

Will they do the unthinkable? If they do manage to win their next two, that final-round contest against Hull KR could be extra tasty...

Sky Sports will show every game of the Super League live this season, including two matches each round exclusively live. The remaining five matches will be broadcast on Sky Sports+ .

articles.title: Rajasthan stuck in 2012, Manipur in 2023: How actively are states with CWG medals promoting sports?
articles.summary: Commonwealth Games News: NEW DELHI: Somewhere on a muddy school field in Haryana right now, a teenager is perhaps drilling the same throwing technique over and over, just as s.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Somewhere on a muddy school field in Haryana right now, a teenager is perhaps drilling the same throwing technique over and over, just as she had watched on television just days ago. Her sole aim is to pull off the one like Sharmila Dhankar, India's Commonwealth Games shot put gold medallist.Before the 2026 CWG campaign, she, like many of us, had almost certainly never heard the name. And it's not because Dhankar had not won anything before the Glasgow Games; she had, a gold medal in the Women's Shot Put F57 event at the 2026 Fazza International Para Athletics Championship, but because one of the primary institutions whose entire job was to carry that story back from the medal podium to villages and training grounds across the state has, for all practical purposes, gone quiet.That's the part of this story that rarely gets told. India walked away from Glasgow with 39 medals, and for a week, the athletes who won them were everywhere, garlanded at airports, seated beside ministers, their faces on the evening news. But medals don't build the next generation of athletes by themselves. Somebody has to keep telling their stories, long after the felicitation photo is filed away, to the kid training in a dusty school ground who needs proof that this path actually leads somewhere.We wanted to know which state sports departments are still doing their job of promoting the sports and their grassroots on their social media platforms, and which ones seem to have simply logged off. So we scrolled through the timelines ourselves. Here's what we found.Haryana: Hit on the podium, not so much off itNo state produced more glory in Glasgow than Haryana. Eleven medallists, including seven gold, two silver, two bronze, spanning boxing, wrestling, athletics, and para sport, headlined by a Neeraj Chopra silver that will be replayed on sports channels for years.Alongside him were names most of India still had little knowledge of. The likes of Preeti Pawar, Jaismine Lamboria, Sakshi Chaudhary, Priya Ghanghas, Sachin Siwach, and Ankush Panghal, all of whom trained in government facilities, under government schemes, and who'd probably appreciate their own state department cheering as loudly for them as it does for its concert lineups.Because that's the thing. The Sports Department, Government of Haryana's X account has posted exactly once in all of 2026, and it's a flyer for the music acts playing at the Chief Minister's Cup.Haryana Sports social media activityFacebook and Instagram follow a similar rhythm with a short cluster of posts around that February event, and then not much else.Eleven medals, and not one dedicated post to show for it. Somewhere in Rohtak or Bhiwani, a young pugilist training in Priya Ghanghas's discipline would probably just like a little proof that someone up top is paying attention.Manipur still talking about 2023Manipur's page has an odd time-capsule quality to it. This is the state that gave India Mirabai Chanu, one of the country's most beloved Olympic medalists, and this Commonwealth Games alone produced four medalists from Manipur, Chanu's gold among them, alongside Rishikanta Singh, Bindyarani Devi, and Jadumani Singh.Manipur Sports social media activityAnd yet the Department of Youth Affairs & Sports' X account hasn't posted since October 2023, a "Run for Unity" event, frozen well before any of this year's medals happened.Although the Facebook page has had a few sporadic posts here and there this year, its Instagram account has managed just two posts since January. Itâs the kind of gap that makes you wonder if someone simply forgot the login details somewhere along the way.Rajasthan: 14 years and countingIf there's one number in this whole exercise worth sitting with, it's this: the official Sports Department, Government of Rajasthan hasn't posted on Facebook since April 14, 2012.Fourteen years, through Arundhati Choudhary's Commonwealth gold and everything else that's happened in Rajasthan sport since.Rajasthan Sports social media activityIts X account's last original post predates a retweet from March 2021, and there's no Instagram at all. A parallel handle, the Rajasthan State Sports Council, exists across all three platforms and is barely livelier.Somewhere behind Choudhary's medal is a genuinely good story, but it just hasn't found a home on the one page built to tell it.Uttar Pradesh and Delhi carry the same gloomy pictureGulveer Singh managed both a silver and a bronze for Uttar Pradesh this Games, a rare double that would make a great centrepiece for the state's sporting year. Instead, across two separate official handles on three platforms, Uttar Pradesh Sports has produced little beyond reposts, while its sister account, Sports Directorate, Govt of Uttar Pradesh, hasn't posted at all in 2026.UP Sports social media activityDelhi Government, for its part, doesn't run a dedicated sports account at all on any of the popular social media platforms, so gold medalist Harsh Singh and bronze medalist Tejaswin Shankar, both representing India's capital, don't really have an institutional cheerleader online, their wins quietly absorbed into the general churn of city government updates. Both athletes are, in effect, doing their own promotional legwork.And then come Tamil Nadu and othersSet against all that quiet, Tamil Nadu feels like a different sport altogether. Its Sports Tamil Nadu handles post multiple times a day, celebrating not just its own three medalists, Praveen Chithravel, Selva Prabhu, Muthupandi Raja, but athletes from other states too, weaving in government scheme updates without it ever reading like bureaucracy.Every medallist got a dedicated post. Somewhere in Tamil Nadu, a kid training in long jump or wrestling doesn't have to wonder whether the sport leads anywhere. The state tells them, publicly, almost daily.Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Karnataka's Facebook and Instagram pages, Assam, Bihar, and Tripura all follow a version of that same habit, active, consistent, generous with attention toward athletes nobody outside their district would otherwise know existed.Kerala doesn't run a separate sports handle on X but keeps its Facebook and Instagram genuinely lively, making sure Murali Sreeshankar and Mohammed Basil's silvers got their due.Andhra Pradesh mirrors that same rhythm across all three platforms.The ones somewhere in the middleNot every state falls neatly into being inactive or staying proactive. Punjab's account managed just two posts on X all year, New Year's and Republic Day, though its Facebook and Instagram carry a bit more life around coaching and departmental meetings, even if athletes rarely get top billing.Uttarakhand was genuinely active last year before cooling off in 2026, leaning more toward government scheme announcements on Facebook, though its Instagram at least carried two posts around the Games.Maharashtra has dedicated posts up for both Sarvesh Kushare and Dilip Gavit, with Instagram staying fairly regular, enough effort to stay out of the quiet column.Karnataka's X account hasn't posted since March 2024, around an unrelated cultural-team event, even though its Facebook and Instagram have stayed warm and active toward its CWG medalists.Does it matter so much?It is worth asking why this actually matters, beyond good manners. Well, a state sports department's social media feed isn't just a courtesy board for congratulations; it's one of the cheapest, most direct tools available to build the next generation of athletes.A youngster in a small town is far more likely to pick up a javelin because they saw a state government post celebrating someone from their own district. Even when it comes to promoting any government policy, social media can be as effective.Visibility drives aspiration. There's a funding logic too. Sponsors, corporates, and even state finance departments allocate resources partly based on visible public interest, and a well-run social account is often the easiest evidence a sport has that interest.ALSO READ: Anahat Singh: What is in the name? A word from Guru Nanak's prayer, now India's squash sensationSilence, on the other hand, sends the message that grassroots sport isn't a priority worth the effort of a single post, even when the state has just produced a medallist on the world stage.It is worth it because sometimes, the first step towards building a sporting culture is simply showing people that their achievements are being seen.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Bangladesh and India battle to save cricket series after political turmoil
articles.summary: Bangladesh and India white-ball series under threat due to tensions that arose when Bangladeshi PM Hasina toppled.
articles.body:
Bangladesh is scrambling to save a six-match cricket tour against neighbouring India next month as the foreign ministers of both nations have been roped in to try to salvage the series.

Comprising three one-day internationals and three T20 matches, the white-ball series was originally planned for August last year but was postponed after diplomatic relations soured between Bangladesh and India.

“We want to quickly resolve the deadlock that was created around the Cricket World Cup,” Haque said.

“God willing, we are hopeful that it will be resolved very soon.”

India last toured Bangladesh for a cricket series in 2022 and won a Test series 2-0. Bangladesh won the ODIs 2-1.

articles.title: Gian van Veen asks for help ahead of New Zealand Darts Masters with bags stuck in Paris
articles.summary: Gian van Veen arrives in Auckland for New Zealand Darts Masters - but bags stuck in Europe; Dutchman asks Qatar Airways for help as he prepares for World Series event at the weekend; Van Veen has just leapfrogged Luke Humphries as world No 2
articles.body:
Van Veen, runner-up to Luke Littler in the 2026 World Darts Championship at Alexandra Palace, has already arrived in Auckland for the event - but his gear has not.

The Dutchman, who has just usurped Luke Humphries as world No 2, wrote on X, tagging Qatar Airways' support page: "I am already in Auckland, but our bags are still at Paris CDG… I will need them before this weekend's World Series tournament. Is there anyone who can help me get them here ASAP?"

Qatar Airways replied to Van Veen, apologising for the mishandled baggage and asking him to contact them directly for further assistance.

articles.title: Bangladesh humble Australia with worst total in contest as Hasan takes 6-55
articles.summary: Australia dismissed for lowest total against Bangladesh as Hasan Mahmud claims career-best on Day One of first Test.
articles.body:
Hasan Mahmud took a career-best 6-55 as Bangladesh bundled Australia out for 198 to take the honours on the opening day of the first Test in Darwin.

At the close on Thursday Bangladesh were 96-1, 102 runs behind Australia.

Mominul Haque was on 35 with Tanzid Hasan alongside him on 32 as the visitors made a superb start to a Test match most people expected them to lose inside three days.

Earlier, Hasan led an impressive display by the visitors’ seamers as Australia slumped to their lowest Test score against Bangladesh, their previous worst being 217 in Mirpur in 2017.

The 26-year-old was the pick of the attack, but he was ably supported by fellow quicks Taskin Ahmed and Ebadot Hossain, who took two wickets apiece.

“I was just trying to bowl line and length, trust the process and follow what the captain was saying,” Hasan said.

“(Taskin and Ebadot) were trying their best and they did very well also.”

Steve Smith was the only Australian to offer any resistance, scoring 71, while the rest of the batsmen looked out of sorts against the disciplined attack.

“We haven’t played a Test match for a while and it can take some time to get into it,” Smith said.

“It wasn’t easy. The ball was doing stuff and you have to be patient.

“Perhaps we got dragged into a few we didn’t need to, but that’s the pressure.”

After skipper Pat Cummins chose to bat on a perfect Darwin day, a full-strength Australia were expected to dominate a Bangladesh side well-beaten by a Cricket Australia XI in their only warm-up match.

Hasan made the initial breakthrough in the 12th over with the score on 45.

Jake Weatherald, on 23, had a huge swipe at a ball outside off stump and only managed a thick edge to wicketkeeper Litton Das.

Hasan struck again soon after, fellow opener Travis Head chopping on for 22 to leave Australia 52-2.

Bangladesh then saw a huge opportunity go begging when Smith, on two, edged Ebadot to third slip where Tanzid Hasan spilled the chance.

Smith had a second escape next over when he got a thick edge off Taskin only for the ball to fly through a vacant third slip.

Marnus Labuschagne, on one, wasn’t so fortunate.

He poked at an Ebadot ball outside off stump and edged to Bangladesh captain Najmul Hossain Shanto at second slip, leaving Australia 61-3.

Cameron Green came in and played some big shots before chipping Taskin to short midwicket, where Mushfiqur Rahim took an easy catch.

Wicketkeeper Alex Carey looked in good touch after lunch and cruised to 19 until he played on to Ebadot with the score on 129.

Taskin then produced the ball of the day to beat Beau Webster’s bat and clip the top off stump to leave the home side struggling on 152-6.

Cummins tried to steer the hosts to tea without further loss; however, Shanto brought Hasan back into the attack with immediate success, the Australian skipper getting a big edge to Litton.

Hasan got his fourth in the same fashion, Mitchell Starc getting a thin edge to the keeper with the score on 172.

Smith threw his wicket away going for a big hit before Nathan Lyon was last man out in similar fashion.

Bangladesh started their reply confidently and eased to 36 before Australia got the breakthrough, Shadman Islam (20) getting a leading edge off Mitchell Starc to Lyon at backward point.

articles.title: The Hundred 2026 awards: Stuart Broad, Nasser Hussain, Lydia Greenway pick best local player, overseas player, newcomer, fielder, captain and more
articles.summary: Nasser Hussain, Stuart Broad, Lydia Greenway pick their best local player, overseas player, newcomer, value for money, fielder, captain for 2026 Hundred season in men and women's competitions
articles.body:
" Jos Buttler is into the eliminator with Manchester Super Giants. Batting three, he's scored vital runs at vital times.

"He's England's best-ever white-ball batter. He's the icon of that MSG franchise.

"He's a leader in that changing room and he's got a chance of lifting the trophy."

" Ben Duckett went straight to the final with Trent Rockets and avoided the eliminator. That's how well he's played.

"Top of the order, he plays spin, plays fast bowling, hits it in unusual areas. He's been brilliant in the field.

"Also, at the top of the order, the way he's set the tone for that middle order of the Trent Rockets, it's just nice to see Duckett playing with such confidence and such flair.

I mentioned his fielding as well, which we do have a section on, but he's been excellent. I'm very impressed."

"I've gone for the leading wicket taker in the tournament, Tilly Corteen-Coleman . I think she's taken 13 wickets.

"The reason I picked her, she's just been really consistent. Not just this season but over the last couple of seasons.

"It's great to see her top of the tree with the wickets."

" Mitch Marsh has played some really eye-catching innings. He's batting at one of the best batting services in the country at Headingley, and he's been really entertaining.

"He's done exactly what you want an overseas player at the top of the order to do. He's led from the front. He's set the tone. He's guided his teams to win.

"His average is higher when they win than when they lose, which means he's playing a key role in winning games. Look at his strike rate, nearly 170.

"So I think he's been really crucial and a really clever signing."

" Mitch Marsh. Compare his consistency to someone like Harry Brook. Now, Harry's a very fine player, but a lot of his runs have come at Headingley on that belter of a surface.

"Mitch Marsh knows Headingley well, he's got Test runs there. He loves it, but he's also gone away from home at Trent Bridge, Manchester. He's got runs all around the country.

"I like the way he's a very simple person. He's a very simple player. You pitch it up, he belts it straight back past you. You drop your length back just a fraction and he'll pull you for six.

"I just love the way he keeps it very simple. And for an Aussie, he's a really nice top bloke."

"Overseas player has to be Phoebe Litchfield . She's obviously the leading run scorer, and the way she's gone out and dominated bowling attacks has been really entertaining to watch.

"She looks as if she's in the form of her life. She's the hardest player to set a field to in the competition.

"She hits straight down the ground, she hits behind square and then she can open up square of the wicket on both sides. She's got that ridiculous switch hit.

"If I was a captain against her, I would literally have no idea where to set the field to. She's absolutely the player in form at the moment."

"Mitch Marsh is new to The Hundred. This is the first year he's played in The Hundred. So if he's new and he's come here from Australia, I have him as a newcomer.

"He had never played a Hundred game before this, I'm taking his age away from it."

"I've gone for a young player who's had his first go, not in franchise cricket but in The Hundred, LD Pretorius .

"No one's really seen him in England, not really heard of him. He's not scored Ashes centuries.

"Pretorius, to me, he's playing on a difficult surface at Lord's, he's played some beautiful shots.

"He's got clear strength through the offside. A pick-up over square leg, which is fantastic.

"He's a really stylish player, and he's one of those newcomers the world of cricket will know a lot of in five years' time."

"I've gone for Charley Phillips . She has come in and really made the most of her opportunity. She's taken some big scalps as well within the seven wickets she's taken.

"And she's bowled in different phases of the game."

"I've gone Calvin Harrison , because he came in late as a replacement player.

"Around about £31,000 was the replacement figure. And he's bowled beautifully. He's got eight wickets.

"He's fielded really well, we've seen some of his extraordinary catches, but I just think to come in at the last moment and play, he's a real talented cricketer.

"That's someone England should be looking at across formats. He bats very well - he hasn't had much chance with the bat because the Trent Rockets have been so good - but value for money, I'm going Calvin Harrison and what he's done for the Trent Rockets."

"I completely agree with Nasser. Calvin Harrison's been absolutely superb and now it's my time to be honest and say I've got this completely wrong with Adil Rashid , because he's on £250k to play!

"Yes, he's been very successful but as Nasser, I think, got newcomer wrong, I might have got value for money wrong because a quarter of a million pounds is quite a lot of money for eight games.

"He's been fantastic, Adil Rashid, as he was going to be.

"He's one of those players that I think every single team would have been talking about at the start of the auction. You know what you're going to get. He just delivers time after time.

"His leg spin, which is always crucial. We're in a dry spell, so it's going to spin a little bit more.

"He's one of those players that could have gone for a lot more. When you're talking about Harry Brook at £465k, Jofra Archer at £450k at the same franchise, that's where I sneaked in my value for money, because he's virtually half the price of Archer, but he performs.

"I've gone for Charley Phillips again here. I think she was a bargain at £15k.

"It's brilliant to see a player like her in the form that she's been in.

"And the wickets that I've mentioned, she's got big wickets. She's got Sophie Devine, Georgia Voll has been in there, Phoebe Litchfield as well, Hollie Armitage.

"So she's just been able to go in, has got quite a slingy action and just hits the top of off-stump. So it's been a pleasure to watch."

" Adil Rashid. Because in an era when spin bowlers have to bowl it quickly, have to bowl it into the surface, I still love the fact that Adil Rashid is brave enough to toss the ball up with all the variations.

"He's right at the top of his game, in an era where spinners sometimes just bowl darts.

" Trent Boult . He's done a few quirky things on the field, celebrations. He particularly upset Jonny Bairstow at Lords, but that was his ball of the tournament for me, the inswinger into the bottom of leg stump.

"I spoke to Jonny and think it was a bit of choice language that sent him off, but that's what Trent does. He's a little bit unusual at times, but he's an incredible bowler.

"I'm just drawn to him. Every time he gets a new ball in his hand, something's going to happen.

"There was a wonderful anti-fist pump that I saw with Mitch Santner. He put it in, Mitch came out, he withdrew it, and it was all a bit awkward, but Trent found that really funny."

"I've gone Nat Sciver-Brunt . The fact she hasn't always played the games, obviously she has been managing that calf injury, but when she comes in she looks as if she's never been away from the game.

"I was watching her in her last game and she wheeled out a reverse sweep first ball and it just shows the class of her, not to just get a score under her belt, but to do it at a decent strike rate.

"She's a player I always enjoy watching. Strong off the back foot, can play little dink shots, but manages the situation, manages the tempo and offers a huge amount obviously for the Rockets."

"I'll fix this a little bit, because Chris Jordan, for me, is the best fielder and has been throughout The Hundred every year, but I just could not leave out this catch from Will Jacks .

"It was Pretorius at the crease, and he was batting really well, and the members were sat watching that right in front of them.

"The first bit of the catch was hard, the second bit was remarkable."

"Catches are easier than run-outs, so that's why I chose this from Ben Duckett .

"A brilliant bit of work from Duckett, diving to his left, picking the ball up, throwing it when he's turning, and most importantly, it doesn't matter if you run out Trent Boult but it does matter if you run out Nicky Pooran.

"A brilliant bit of work to hit the stumps when you only have one to aim at. I thought that really changed that game."

"I've gone for Bess Heath actually. In terms of number of catches, she isn't up there, but I love her approach.

"For any young girl, if you're at a ground and you're watching Heath, you can tell she's got that mentality of wanting the ball to come to her.

"She doesn't shy away from catches. She made one absolutely stunning catch. A lot of players would have sat back, they would have let it bounce once and would have taken the ball and it wouldn't have even been an opportunity.

"She's been a real sort of entertainer and energetic person in the field, which adds so much value to a team when you're out there."

"Sam Billings. He's won the last three Hundred titles with Oval Invincibles, he's gone to Trent Rockets, and first of all it was a brilliant signing from Trent Rockets, knowing his leadership capability.

"Once he's been given the role at a ground that he's not captained in a huge amount at before, Trent Bridge, he's got to know what the crowd like, he's got to know the surface very well.

"He leads his players brilliantly, they're top of the table, deserve to be top of the table, straight to the final, which was always the goal for the Trent Rockets, and he's got a hell of a chance to go four from four."

" Sam Billings . I like his aggression and the fact he's got a point to prove.

"He did an interview after he beat MI London - he was there for three years and unceremoniously sacked by them, let's be honest, after everything he'd done - and he's gone to his next franchise and he's proving a point.

"He loves this tournament. It's almost the latter stages of his career, it's what makes Sam Billings the cricketer he is."

"I've actually gone for Dani Gibson because if people remember the SunRisers Leeds went on a run of three losing games. They couldn't get a win for love nor money, but she and her team managed to turn it around.

"They're now finding some form at a really good time.

"For someone like Dani Gibson, it's the first time she's captain in a tournament on this sort of stage, so I've loved how she's done it.

"I love how she's spoken to the media and just the energy that she brings on the field.

"Tactically, clearly she'll always be learning. She's obviously got Adrian Birrell, who she's working closely with as a head coach. I've really enjoyed watching her this season."

articles.title: England bolters: The names putting their hand up despite not being in performance squad with Umyla Hanley, Tom Holroyd included
articles.summary: England will head to the Rugby League World Cup in Australia in October; Brian McDermott will be tasked with choosing a squad to go; 38-man performance squad was announced in June
articles.body:
Back in June, new England head coach Brian McDermott announced a 38-man performance squad, including 10 uncapped players, with whom he would work over the season to get England as well prepared as they can be for the tournament come October.

Leeds Rhinos star and reigning Man of Steel Jake Connor has not played for his country in seven years and was overlooked by then England coach Shaun Wane for the 3-0 Ashes defeat at home to Australia last autumn. But now, he is back.

The 10 newbies include Wakefield Trinity's Jake Trueman and Caleb Hamlin-Uele, Wigan Warriors' Sam Walters and Zach Eckersley, Hull KR's Dean Hadley and St Helens' Harry Robertson.

But is all hope lost for those not in those 38 names? Could some players make a late surge?

Let's take a look at who has been playing their way into potentially being a late bolter for England...

Tom Holroyd has hit incredible form in the middle-to-late stages of this season and has become the definition of super-sub.

His physicality and impact has been clear for all to see and indeed, even his head coach Brad Arthur believes he has to be considered for a place on the plane if England want a point of difference. Arthur also touted Cameron Smith for a place too.

"I think Cameron (Smith) and Tom are showing off the bench that they could provide a really good option for that team," Arthur said.

"Tom, with his impact and his aggression, and Cameron - he comes on, and he can just change the point of attack with his footwork, his pass, and his offload.

"And I just think if you're going to try and beat Australia, you're not going to be able to defend your way to victory; you're going to need to be able to score points and both of those guys can help with that."

England have a lot of options in the middle but you would not be shocked if Holroyd is on the radar now too.

Since returning from injury, Umyla Hanley has really been impressing for Leigh Leopards, especially in attack.

Indeed, he was included in the Man of Steel panels considerations for the middle part of the season then was key in Leigh's massive win over Leeds in round 23.

Similarly to Arthur with Holroyd, Leigh head coach Adrian Lam has gone into bat for his man and believes that he has a big international future ahead of him.

"That tackle that he made at the end of the game on Ryan Hall to get his foot across the line- if anyone had said to me, 'someone's going to save you a try at the end of the game' - I would have said it was him, and all of his team-mates would have said it was him," Lam said.

"He's the ultimate competitor I've coached. No, he's the number one player I've coached in my life that competes better than anyone, and I challenge that to anyone in Super League."

Speak to any Wigan fan and they will tell you how integral Oliver Partington has been in their 2026 Super League campaign.

A work horse, he does all the hard yards that make someone the ultimate team-mate and he is willing to put his hand up for anything.

They say that what matters in big games are not the sparkling moments but the effort areas and Partington excels in those every single time.

While he will have a lot of competition in his position, he is someone who has been a standout in 2026.

Yes, he is not in Super League but it would be remiss of me to overlook Matty Nicholson.

He has returned for the last couple of games off the bench for the Raiders and if he finds a run of form, he will be someone very much in McDermott's thinking.

The new England boss has said he will firmly have eyes on the NRL as well as Super League and with that in mind, Nicholson has a real chance to get back into the international scene.

England 38-man performance programme group :

Junior Nsemba, Ethan Havard, Luke Thompson, Sam Walters, Brad O'Neill, Jake Wardle, Harry Smith, Zach Eckersley (all Wigan Warriors), Kallum Watkins, Mikolaj Oledzki, Ash Handley, Jake Connor (all Leeds Rhinos), Ben Currie, Danny Walker, George Williams, Matty Ashton (all Warrington Wolves), Kai Pearce-Paul (Wests Tigers), Dean Hadley, Jez Litten, Mikey Lewis (all Hull KR), Morgan Smithies, Jayden Brailey (both Canberra Raiders), Victor Radley, Billy Smith (both Sydney Roosters), AJ Brimson (Gold Coast Titans), Jack Welsby, Alex Walmsley, Daryl Clark, Harry Robertson (all St Helens), Morgan Knowles, Herbie Farnworth (both Dolphins), Mike McMeeken, Caleb Hamlin-Uele, Jake Trueman, Tom Johnstone (all Wakefield), Matt King (Canterbury Bulldogs), Ben Talty (Brisbane Broncos), Dom Young (Newcastle Knights).
